name: Job
description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs

points: There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job. And that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God and eschewed evil. And there were born unto him seven sons and three daughters. He has seven sons, three daughters. Good.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows

points: This first verse tells you who Job is, what land he lived in, and his character. Just because he lived in the land of Uz does not mean he was of that nation, because he was a son of God.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

points: And it was so, when the days of their feasting were gone about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all — meaning ten.
For Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.
Now, there is something very odd about that. Job was sending up sacrifices, saying, perhaps my sons have sinned. Job knew exactly what his kids were doing. Watch.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows

points: Everyone his day means their birthday. Job sanctified his children and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all, for Job said, it may be that my sons have sinned and cursed God in their hearts. He knew what his sons were doing. Thus did Job continually.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

points: His sons went and feasted, every one his day: birthdays. Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. The only time we read about birthdays in the scriptures, the heathens kept them; that's for those of you still celebrating your date of birth on the low.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

points: Job was perfect and upright, feared God and eschewed evil, and was the greatest man in the east. His sons feasted every one his day, and Job sanctified them and offered burnt offerings in case they had sinned and cursed God in their hearts.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

points: Job sanctified them and rose up early to offer burnt offerings according to the number of them all, for Job said it may be that his sons had sinned and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

points: Job's life is a template for what each one of us will have to go through.

note.label: Born for Adversity

points: The hedge about Job, his house and all he had was angels. Satan wanted Job but could not get to him. The Lord removed the hedge and gave all Job had into Satan's power, but not his life. God has a say in how far Satan goes.
Job lost all ten children in one wind and still fell down and worshipped: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away. Would you still bless the Lord knowing he allowed Satan to do it?

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

points: This is Satan talking to the Lord. The Lord says, have you considered My servant Job, have you ever tried Job, you walking up and down the earth, have you tried My servant, because he is an upright man.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

points: In Christianity they teach that Satan and God had a fight and Satan rebelled and took a third of the angels. That does not sound like what is right here. Job was the subject of discussion between Satan and the Lord, and Satan needed permission from the Lord to mess with him.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

points: Job still held fast his integrity, and Satan is called the one who moved the Lord against him without cause. That is the accuser at work, as Revelation 12 names him.
The deacon promises at least five classes on how to fight Satan, with the last on another level, and a separate class on the different ways Satan attacked Job.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

points: Again there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also. The Lord said, hast thou considered My servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, and still he holdeth fast his integrity, although thou movedst Me against him to destroy him without cause.
The Lord is bragging, He is boasting: even though you made Me go after Job for no reason at all, he is still standing strong, he is still handling his business.

note.label: Job 2: Skin for Skin

points: And the Lord said unto Satan, Behold, he is in thine hand; but save his life. So Satan smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown: the fifth trial, Job's health in decline.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

points: Satan went forth and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown, and Job took a potsherd to scrape himself withal, and he sat down among the ashes.

note.label: Job 2: Skin for Skin

points: But he said, thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips. He upheld his integrity even through trials and tribulations, when things are inconvenient.

note.label: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

points: Job said, thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh; what, shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips.

note.label: Job 2: Skin for Skin

points: Job's three friends heard of all this evil that came upon him: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. They made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him.

note.label: Job 2: Skin for Skin

points: After this Job opened his mouth and cursed his day. Why did he curse his day? Because his children were celebrating their day, and Job cursed the day he was born.

Job is going in on his birthday. That is why we say to hell with our birthday, our birthday means nothing. The scriptures say better is the day of one's death than the day of one's birth, because when you are born there are no works yet; when you die that is when people remember your works and what kind of person you were.

note.label: Job 3: Job Curses His Day

points: Remember verse 1 says Job continued his parable. A lot of what Job is talking about, not the entire book but a lot of it, is in parable form, and most of it is above the pay grade.

note.label: Job 29: The Days When The Most High Preserved Me

points: If his land cried against him or its furrows complained, if he ate its fruits without money or caused its owners to lose their life, then let thistles grow instead of wheat and cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.

note.label: Job 31: The Words Of Job Are Ended

points: The three men ceased to answer Job because he was righteous in his own eyes, and Elihu's wrath was kindled because Job justified himself rather than God. Job said he was not weak like Adam. That was his flaw: he was over-righteous.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

points: These three men ceased to answer Job because he was righteous in his own eyes. Then the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram, was kindled against Job because he justified himself rather than God.

note.label: Job 32: The Wrath Of Elihu The Young Man

points: Elihu's wrath was also kindled against the three friends because they found no answer and yet condemned Job. Elihu had waited until Job had spoken because they were elder than he. This is a young man, and in this chapter alone you learn a lot about how young men should be with men that are aged, especially wise men in this truth.

note.label: Job 32: The Wrath Of Elihu The Young Man

points: Elihu tells Job to mark well, hearken, and hold his peace while Elihu speaks, and if Job has anything to say, to answer, for Elihu desires to justify him.
If not, Job is to hold his peace and Elihu will teach him wisdom.

note.label: Job 33: Elihu Speaks God's Instruction to Man

points: Elihu recounts that Job said he is righteous and that God has taken away his judgment, that his wound is incurable without transgression.

note.label: Job 34: God Renders to Every Man According to His Ways

points: He asks what man is like Job, who drinks up scorning like water, goes in company with the workers of iniquity, and says it profits a man nothing to delight himself with God.

note.label: Job 34: God Renders to Every Man According to His Ways

points: Men of understanding tell Elihu that Job has spoken without knowledge and his words were without wisdom.

note.label: Job 34: God Renders to Every Man According to His Ways

points: Elihu's desire is that Job may be tried unto the end because of his answers for wicked men, for he added rebellion unto his sin, clapped his hands among them, and multiplied his words against God.

note.label: Job 34: God Renders to Every Man According to His Ways

points: Hearken unto this, O Job; stand still and consider the wondrous works of God. Consider the wondrous works of Him which is perfect in knowledge, how thy garments are warm when He quieteth the earth by the south wind.

note.label: Job 37: The Works of the Most High

points: This is the Lord talking to Job. Before, in the previous chapter, it was Elihu speaking; now the Most High Himself steps in.

note.label: Job 38: Where Wast Thou

points: The thing is we get so high-minded sometimes, because of the little bit of knowledge that we have out of this Bible, and the wicked still rule over us. You better humble yourself. That is the whole purpose of the book of Job: learning how to humble yourself.

note.label: Job 40: Humble Thyself Before the Most High

points: After the Most High had spoken these words, He tells Eliphaz the Temanite that His wrath is kindled against him and his two friends, because they have not spoken of Him the thing that is right, as His servant Job has. Throughout the book Job's three friends dealt wrongly with him after his children were killed and everything was taken, so they did not deal righteously as their brother Job did.

note.label: Job 42: The Lord Turned the Captivity of Job

points: He commands them to take seven bullocks and seven rams and go to Job and offer a burnt offering for themselves, and Job will pray for them, for him will He accept, lest He deal with them after their folly. The sacrifice for their sin had to be brought to Job, the righteous one in the situation.

note.label: Job 42: The Lord Turned the Captivity of Job

points: This is how the priesthood worked, all the way from Leviticus and the five books throughout history: we brought the sacrifice to the Levites and priests and they did it on our behalf, and if a man did not bring his sacrifice, the Most High would deal with him and what he did would not be forgiven. Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the Most High commanded, and He accepted Job.

note.label: Job 42: The Lord Turned the Captivity of Job

points: The Most High turned the captivity of Job when he prayed for his friends, and gave him twice as much as he had before. It was not the prayer alone that availed, but the prayer of a righteous man, so the Most High deals with those that are dealing in righteousness.

note.label: Job 42: The Lord Turned the Captivity of Job

points: The Most High blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses, along with seven sons and three daughters. He named the daughters Jemima, Kezia, and Keren-happuch, and in all the land were no women found so fair, and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.

The purpose of the trial was to see whether Job would fix himself and stay faithful or curse the Most High. The same thing happens to us: we endure to the end as Job did, and at some point the Most High will turn the captivity of the Israelites who kept the commandments and repay them for all their righteousness, far more than double the houses, families, cars, and jobs we have now, giving us much more in the kingdom.

note.label: Job 42: The Lord Turned the Captivity of Job

points: Job lived an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons' sons, even four generations. The generation here is talking about his descendants: your son, your grandson, your great grandson, your great great grandson. That is genealogical generation.

note.label: The Plagues Coming to America

points: Job lived a hundred and forty years after this and saw his sons and his sons' sons, even four generations, and died being old and full of days. He received much more than he had in the beginning, all because he stayed faithful to the Most High through the whole trial.

note.label: Job 42: The Lord Turned the Captivity of Job

points: Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness. That's what Noah did, his wife did, his sons did, and their wives did: saved themselves by their own righteousness. Likewise Daniel, likewise Job.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

points: Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness.

note.label: Ezekiel 14: Idols in the Heart and the Four Sore Judgments
